issues.title: Decode profile (RTX A3000 + i7-12850HX): the CPU expert pool is ~half the round; pin the verify host first
issues.author: yannickloth
issues.body:
## Context

A decode-time profile of the RTX A3000 12 GB laptop + i7-12850HX host from #485, on production engine **0.1.35**
(Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS native pack, the calibrated `--pcie-frac 0.35 --spec-min-p 0.70
--pool-workers 8`), from the engine's own `--stats` accumulators. Full write-up and raw lines:
`bench/results/2026-10-02-rtx-a3000-i7-12850hx/profile.md` (PR #489).

## The split

One verify-window round, ms and share of the round's wall clock. A round emits 2.10 tokens at the fresh hit
rate and 1.15 when the output degenerates and hits more.

| Term | fresh decode, `hit_rate 0.354` | ms | warm/degenerate, `hit_rate 0.756` | ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| GPU — "wait for rings" | 34% | 26.7 | 62% | 23.1 |
| CPU expert pool | **53%** | 41.6 | 26% | 9.6 |
| MTP drafter | 4% | 3.1 | 6% | 2.1 |
| host | 2% | 1.7 | 1% | 0.2 |
| verify copy-stream commit | ~0% | 0.03 | ~0% | 0.03 |
| embed/sample/round overhead | 6% | 4.9 | 6% | 2.2 |
| round | | 78.1 (26.9 tok/s) | | 37.3 (30.9 tok/s) |

Real serve traffic on this host ran `hit_rate 0.35-0.65` (34-40 tok/s), i.e. the fresh-decode end. There the
**CPU expert pool is the largest single term**, and the GPU is second.

## What it sizes

- **Pinning the verify host thread is the top host-side lever.** The pool is 26-53% of the round; recovering the
  `pool.hpp` pinned vs in-loop rates (36.3 vs 26.9 GB/s, ~1.35×) is worth ~+8-15% tok/s. The pool measures only
  **18-22 GB/s over the rows** here, so there may be more than 1.35× to win. The `generate`/session path already
  pins the host (`SessionLoopScratch::init`), but the serve/spec `Verifier::run` does not — the doorbell-spinning
  host and the PCIe-copy helpers are free to land on a worker's core.
- **256-bit AVX-VNNI is bounded.** The down path is ~29% of the pool; a 1.5-2× down path is ~5-8% of the round.
  The i-quant gate/up is ~68% of the pool and documented codebook-bound, so VNNI barely touches it.
- **The per-window copy-stream `cudaStreamSynchronize` is already ~0 ms/round on this host.** The MTP drafter's
  per-draft syncs live inside the 4-6% MTP term and are the only part of that area with headroom.
- **P/E-aware division:** `--pool-workers 8` on the default `--pool-affinity all` does **not** land on 8 P-cores;
  it pins cores `2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16` = seven P-core primaries + the first E-core, and the E-core is the tail of
  every split-row drain. `--pool-affinity p-cores` avoids it but starts only `p_cores - 1 = 7` workers.

## Notes for measuring this model

The native IQ pack runs verify windows only, so `--gpu-stages`, `--gpu-only-full` and `--no-pool`+`--spec` are
unavailable (`session_replay_stages: not captured with the split`, etc.), and `/metrics`'
`ram_blobs`/`file_blobs`/`file_mb` are 0 on the `MAP_HUGETLB` arena. The verify-window "wait for rings" term is
the GPU floor available on this path; the 26.32 ms graph floor is the non-native path's.

Refs #485 (the probe's low reading matters via `pcie_frac`, not via bandwidth: PCIe in use is ~4 GB/s) and #487.

issues.title: [2x RTX 2080 Ti ] 262K context can OOM the weight arena / hard-freeze host; 204800 is stable
issues.author: wxaef
issues.body:
# [Linux][2x RTX 2080 Ti] 262K context can OOM the weight arena / hard-freeze host; 204800 is stable

## Summary

On a Linux system with **2× RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB** using a layer split, a 262144-token context can exhaust VRAM during startup / allocation and, in the worst case, make the whole machine stop responding. Reducing the context to **204800** makes the same setup stable.

The concrete allocation failure I observed was:

```text
cudaMalloc(1538035200) weight arena failed
```

This was with **IQ3_XXS + vision enabled**. Because the failure can hard-freeze the host, I have not deliberately reproduced it again on 0.1.35 yet. I checked the 0.1.35 changes; #448 improves prompt-chunk diagnostics for split GPUs, but it does not appear to change this allocation path.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- RAM: 126 GB
- CPU: AVX-2, no AVX-512
- GPU: 2× NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti 22 GB
- Interconnect: NVLink (NV2)
- GPU topology: both GPUs on CPU affinity 0-23
- Model: Swift 1.5 / Qwen3.8 Flash-Next GSQ-RCO **IQ3_XXS**
- Vision: enabled
- Layer split: auto, CUDA0 then CUDA1
- KV: int8
- KV resident: 32768
- Speculation: 4
- PCIe fraction: 0.35
- Spec min p: 0.70
- Pool workers: 9

The machine normally runs near full GPU utilization during generation.

## Reproduction shape

Problematic configuration:

```text
--context 262144
--kv int8
--kv-resident 32768
--spec 4
--spec-min-p 0.70
--pcie-frac 0.35
--pool-workers 9
--vision
--layer-split auto
```

With IQ3_XXS, this reached a point where a ~1.43 GiB device allocation failed:

```text
cudaMalloc(1538035200) weight arena failed
```

On at least one run, the system became effectively unresponsive rather than failing cleanly.

## Stable comparison

The same machine is stable with:

```text
--context 204800
--prefill 4096
--reserve 1800
--kv int8
--kv-resident 32768
--spec 4
--spec-min-p 0.70
--pcie-frac 0.35
--pool-workers 9
```

So the practical boundary on this machine is somewhere between ~205K and 262K with this model / vision / split configuration.

## Why this seems worth guarding

At 262K the combined VRAM consumers include:

- dense/model weights
- expert cache
- streamed/resident KV
- prefill buffers
- MTP/speculative buffers
- vision allocations
- CUDA workspace / weight arena

The engine can apparently commit enough of these earlier allocations that a later large weight-arena allocation fails. On this hardware the failure can be severe enough to make the host unusable.

## Request

Could Strata do one or more of the following?

1. **Budget the late weight-arena / workspace allocation before committing the expert cache / other large VRAM users**, especially with vision + layer split.
2. Keep a larger automatic safety margin when `--max-context` is very large.
3. If the requested context cannot fit safely, **fail before loading / allocating everything**, with a message suggesting a lower context such as 204800.
4. If possible, make allocation failure recover cleanly instead of leaving the GPU / host in a state that can hard-freeze Linux.
5. Log a compact per-GPU VRAM budget before the risky allocation (weights, expert cache, KV resident, prefill/workspace, vision, reserve), which would make this much easier to diagnose.

I can test a patch or provide a full startup log if there is a specific tracing flag you want enabled.

## Note about 0.1.35

I saw the new #448 diagnostics around prompt-chunk borrowing and split-card cache constraints. My GPUs are symmetric 22 GB cards, and this failure is a later `cudaMalloc(... weight arena ...)` OOM rather than the small-secondary-GPU prompt-chunk case, so I don't think #448 addresses this particular failure.

issues.title: PCIe probe can read ~3x low and pin pcie_frac far below the calibrated value
issues.author: yannickloth
issues.body:
`probe_pcie_h2d_gbps()` (`src/program/generate.cpp`) measures one 256 MiB x4 pinned burst after a single warmup and derives `pcie_frac` from it. On the same machine the same binary read the link at very different rates across starts, and a low sample pins `pcie_frac` well below what `tools/calibrate.py` picks.

## Environment

- NVIDIA RTX A3000 12 GB Laptop (sm_86), PCIe **x16 Gen4** (`current_link_width=16`, `16.0 GT/s`)
- Intel Core i7-12850HX (8 P + 8 E, AVX2, no AVX-512), 128 GB RAM
- Engine 0.1.34, native IQ3_XXS pack (39.97 GiB arena)

## Measurements (same host, across starts)

```
PCIe probe: 18.5 GB/s host->device -> pcie_frac 0.39 (default 0.55)
PCIe probe:  6.9 GB/s host->device -> pcie_frac 0.15 (default 0.55)
PCIe probe:  5.8 GB/s host->device -> pcie_frac 0.12 (default 0.55)
```

`tools/calibrate.py` on the same host (decode tok/s, `--spec-min-p` fixed):

| `--pcie-frac` | 0.0 | 0.2 | 0.35 | 0.55 | 0.75 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| tok/s | 27.0 | 30.1 | **32.7** | 32.5 | 30.8 |

So the auto value the probe produced (0.12-0.15) is ~5 tok/s below the calibrated 0.35, and 0.35 also edges out the 0.55 default.

## Likely cause

One 256 MiB x4 burst (1 GiB) after one warmup, on the default stream, with no retry/median and no exclusivity check: concurrent copy-engine work, ASPM/low link power state, or a context that has not ramped can depress the single sample, and the result is then used as a hard tuning input.

## Suggested fix

Prime the link and take the median of several bursts (a host-side fix is on the `fix/pcie-probe-median` branch of my fork), and/or read the trained link width/speed (NVML `nvmlDeviceGetCurrPcieLinkWidth` / `...LinkSpeed`) instead of one bandwidth sample. Note also the `bw / 26` formula's discontinuity at 20 GB/s (19.9 -> 0.42, 20.0 -> 0.55), which a noisy sample can straddle.

A full write-up of this host (hugepages, probe, calibration) is in `bench/results/2026-10-02-rtx-a3000-i7-12850hx/`.

issues.title: serve engine deadlocks in SleepConditionVariableSRW during a long streaming reply; stall watchdog never fires
issues.author: gu-feng
issues.body:
## Environment

- **Engine:** 0.1.34 ready-made release build (`BUILD.json`: version 0.1.34, source "release", portable, cuda 13.0, archs 75/86/89/120), `engine\strata.exe` timestamp 2026-10-02 00:55 UTC. Observed twice live on this exact build. The 0.1.35 changelog doesn't list anything matching this, so I assume it is still present (not yet re-tested on 0.1.35).
- **Hardware:** NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120) — the only CUDA device; Intel i5-14600K (6 P-cores + 8 E-cores, no AVX-512); 64 GB RAM; Windows 11 Pro build 26200.
- **Serve:** `serve/server.py`, OpenAI-compatible endpoint on 127.0.0.1:8080.
- **Engine args** (one line for easy re-use):

```
--pack <packs\iq3_xxs> --native <shard1> --ple-gguf <shard2> --expert-profile <custom profile> --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --mtp <mtp\rt> --max-context 205824 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision --vram-reserve-mib 700 --pcie-frac 0.35 --spec-min-p 0.70 --pool-workers 9 --pool-affinity auto
```

(`--pool-affinity auto` was added between the two live observations; the first deadlock predates it, so affinity is not implicated.)

- **Client:** an agentic coding client over OpenAI-compatible SSE: tool-call loops, 34K–85K-token prompts with heavy prefix reuse, `reasoning_effort: high` → multi-minute `<think>` streams, occasional client-side cancels.

## What happens

Mid-generation, the engine **deadlocks**: output stops, the GPU drops to 0% while VRAM stays allocated (15.1 GB held), the engine process's total CPU time freezes (every thread blocked), and the request never completes nor errors. The client hangs until the whole service is restarted. The engine log's last line is always a normally-completed earlier request — nothing is written at the moment of the hang, on stderr or stdout.

Happened 4+ times over two days, **only** with this agentic client; browser chat and short requests never trigger it. Both live-observed cases froze ~74 s into a `<think>` stream (once at thinking token 2459, once at 9717+).

## Evidence (second occurrence, captured live)

1. Engine process 12+ minutes into the freeze: all 30 threads in `Wait` (2× `EventPairLow`, rest `Unknown`/`UserRequest`), total CPU time identical across samples.
2. Full memory dump taken (`comsvcs MiniDump /full`), parsed without symbols. **Main thread:**

```
ntdll.dll!NtWaitForAlertByThreadId+0x14            <- RIP
ntdll.dll!RtlSleepConditionVariableSRW+0x1de
KERNELBASE.dll!SleepConditionVariableSRW+0x38
strata.exe+0x35f118                                <- caller of SleepConditionVariableSRW
```

The dump was deleted after analysis (64 GB), but I can reproduce, re-dump and pull **all 30 thread stacks** with a working minidump parser if that helps identify the lock partner.
3. **The stall watchdog never fires.** After 12+ minutes of a fully frozen process there was no `no progress for ... s ... (issue #29)` line and no `strata-stall-<pid>.dmp`. Whatever the main thread waits on, the watchdog's progress accounting does not cover it.
4. **`serve/server.py` wedges with the engine.** After I force-killed the deadlocked engine process, the server did not respawn it on the next request (the request handler stays stuck); only restarting the whole server recovers.

## Ruled out

- **RAM/VRAM exhaustion:** memtest86 clean; the wedge reproduced with ~24 GB RAM free; engine VRAM was at its planned steady state (520 MiB free, no `LOW` warning) — and the deadlock is a permanent wait, not a slowdown.
- **GPU driver TDR:** no Event 4101 / LiveKernelEvent at the freeze times.
- **The client's cancels as the direct trigger of the *freeze*** — a cancel was in flight around the first incident, but the second freeze happened with no cancel; cancelled requests complete cleanly otherwise (v0.1.34's fast cancel works).

## Frequency / repro shape

Every occurrence: long agentic session (tool calls + big reused prefixes) with `reasoning_effort: high` → a thinking stream several minutes long → engine freezes mid-stream. Never in ~50 short chat/browser requests. I cannot reproduce it on demand yet, but it recurs within a day of agentic use.

## Asks

1. Resolve `strata.exe+0x35f118` in the 0.1.34 release build (a `.pdb`/map for release builds — or a hint which `std::condition_variable::wait` in the serve path sits there — would let me self-resolve and give you the function).
2. Why the stall watchdog (`STRATA_WATCHDOG_S`) doesn't cover this wait; ideally a stuck engine should still self-report and dump.
3. `serve/server.py`: detect a dead (or force-killed) engine mid-request and respawn, instead of wedging the handler.

## Workaround I run meanwhile

An external scheduled task tails the server's stdout (Tee-Object to a file) and restarts the whole service when a `[strata] thinking:` progress line goes stale for >90 s. Turns the hang into a ~2 min hiccup.

Happy to attach: per-thread stack dump of all 30 threads on the next occurrence, `STRATA_TRACE=1` log through a freeze, or the engine + server logs around either incident.

issues.title: Persist the runtime expert heat map across restarts; optionally select a profile per working directory
issues.author: AXKore
issues.body:
What the engine already does
At startup, GPU expert residency is seeded from the shipped static profile (data/expert-profile.bin), then refined at runtime by --adapt-every as real token traffic is observed.
Measured on my side (RTX 4090 24 GB, IQ3_S, 262K context): the decode cache hit rate climbs 63% → 73% → 85% within the first requests, and long agent sessions then hold a much higher sustained decode rate (65-75 tok/s, MTP draft acceptance 65-84%).
The gap
Everything learned since engine start lives only in RAM. On restart, the engine falls back to the generic shipped profile, and the first minutes of every session are spent re-learning my usage pattern from scratch.

Proposal — three levels, each independently useful
Persist the learned residency. Save the runtime heat map on clean exit (or periodically) and reload it at start instead of the shipped profile — e.g. --expert-profile-save <path> paired with the existing --expert-profile <path>. A cold start becomes warm.
Per-context selection. The engine already accepts a profile file at start, so launchers could pick one per working directory (code vs prose vs a specific codebase — the token distribution of a project is a signature, and different projects heat different experts). Only the save side from (1) is missing to make this possible.
Later: opt-in sharing/blending of profiles. They are small (KB-scale), so per-user or per-domain profiles ("Python coder", "FR writer"…) could be exchanged. A profile is a usage fingerprint, though, so this should stay strictly opt-in.
Why it fits the current design
The load path exists today; the runtime measurement exists today. This is only save + selection built around them.
Staleness risk is minimal: --adapt-every still refines at runtime, so an outdated profile is simply a better-than-generic prior, never a wrong answer.
Great fit for agent workloads (Claude Code and friends), where engines get restarted often and the first minutes matter.
Note
Keeping the save feature off by default (or local-only) seems right, since profiles reflect what a user works on.

Environment: engine 0.1.34, Windows 11, RTX 4090, Ryzen 9 5950X, 128 GB RAM, IQ3_S packed install.

issues.title: strata serve: mtp: the draft head does not fit — no guidance when MTP draft head exceeds VRAM on smaller GPUs
issues.author: saikiran121111
issues.body:
What happened

The engine crashes on startup with this error when the MTP draft layer's token-subset head can't fit in VRAM:

strata serve: mtp: the draft head does not fit
RuntimeError: the engine exited before it was ready

This is a silent failure — the user gets no hint about what to change. On a 12 GB RTX 3060 with IQ3_S at 262K context, only ~1,500 MiB is free when MTP tries to bind; the default CJK draft vocab (106K tokens) needs ~348 MiB of contiguous VRAM and fails.

The fix already exists but isn't surfaced

setup.py and setup.sh already accept --draft-vocab with three choices:

┌───────────────┬─────────┬─────────────────┐
 │    choice     │ tokens  │ draft head VRAM │
├───────────────┼─────────┼─────────────────┤
│cjk (default) │ 106,299 │ ~348 MiB        │
├───────────────┼─────────┼─────────────────┤
│     cyrillic      │ 57,793  │      ~189 MiB        │
├───────────────┼─────────┼─────────────────┤
│       en            │ 40,525  │       ~133 MiB        │
└───────────────┴─────────┴─────────────────┘

Switching to --draft-vocab en resolved it immediately. The issue is that setup picks the default without considering VRAM headroom, and the engine's error message doesn't mention the flag.

Two small improvements that would help

1. Engine: when MTP's bind() fails with "the draft head does not fit", print a hint: "Try a smaller draft vocabulary: --draft-vocab en (English/code, ~110 MiB less VRAM) or --draft-vocab cyrillic. Change it in setup with --draft-vocab."
2. Setup / engine startup: when --vram-reserve-mib leaves less headroom than the draft head needs, pick en (or cyrillic) automatically and note it, rather than silently using the largest vocab regardless of GPU size.
3. setup.sh / START-HERE.bat: mention --draft-vocab as a tuning option for GPUs under 14 GB VRAM.

Environment

- Strata engine v0.1.34, model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, context 262144
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 12 GB
- OS: Linux

issues.title: A prompt cancelled mid-read is logged and recorded as fully read (wrong tok/s, full size in DONE//metrics)
issues.author: homeofe
issues.body:
A request cancelled during its prompt read is logged, and recorded in `DONE` / `/metrics`, as if the **whole** prompt had been read. The prompt-read rate it prints is therefore far too high.

## Seen (engine 0.1.33, CUDA, RTX 2080 Ti, IQ3_S, `--prefill auto` → 3,072-token chunks)

A streaming request with a fresh ~98K-token prompt. The client hangs up ~10 s in, and the engine stops after 4 chunks (12,288 tokens, 17.5 s after the request was sent):

```
strata serve: prompt 98179 tokens = 0 reused + 98179 read in 17565 ms (5589.6 tok/s), 0 generated in 0 ms (0.0 tok/s), drafts accepted 0 of 0, 0 checkpoints (cancelled)
strata serve: KV streaming: 100.00% of 0 block reads hit VRAM, 0.0 MiB read from RAM
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 18 s (0.0 tok/s) (disconnect, cancel=True), ...
```

- **Tokens read:** only 12,288 were read (the `live.prompt_read` progress in `/metrics` showed it). This card reads ~690 tok/s at that depth, not 5,590.
- **History:** `/metrics` history records the request with the full 98,179-token prompt.
- **Runs:** the same in 6 of 6 runs (3 streaming, 3 non-streaming).

## Where

`src/program/generate.cpp` (main, ~5567-5582). The `DONE` record and the `strata serve: prompt …` line use `n` (the request's prompt length), and `fresh = n - resume`, whether or not the request was cancelled. `cancelled` only appends ` (cancelled)`.

## Suggestion

When `cancelled`, report the tokens actually read: the position the prompt pass reached, something like `… = 0 reused + 12288 of 98179 read in 17565 ms (699.6 tok/s) … (cancelled)`, and either pass that count in `DONE` or mark the record so the server doesn't count it as a full prompt. I'm not sending a PR because the right semantics for `DONE` (prompt length vs. tokens processed, and what the server's prefix cache assumes after a cancel) are your call. I'm happy to make the change once you say which.

The data comes from measuring #431 on CUDA. The server there ran 0.1.33 plus the #430 change from #436, not 0.1.34's watcher, but this log path is the same on `main`.

issues.title: v0.1.34 Windows AMD (discrete W7900): crash 0xC0000005 on first request — engine loads the driver's System32 amdhip64_7.dll
issues.author: phntsm408
issues.body:
**What happens**
Fresh clone of v0.1.34, set up with `START-HERE.bat --setup --backend hip --low-ram on`. The engine loads fine (all 24,576 experts in the GPU cache), then crashes on the very first request with exit code 3221225477 (0xC0000005). It happens every time, on every model.

**Cause**
The crash is inside `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\amdhip64_7.dll` (the AMD driver's HIP runtime, 10.0.3683.0), called from the bundled `engine\rocm\bin\rocblas.dll` via `hipblasGemmEx`. Windows' DLL search order picks the driver's System32 runtime ahead of the bundled ROCm, so the bundled rocBLAS/hipBLAS run on a mismatched HIP runtime.

Stack (top):
    #0  amdhip64_7.dll+0x2d874a (C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32)
    #6  rocblas_zgemv (engine\rocm\bin\rocblas.dll)
    #11 rocblas_gemm_ex
    #12 hipblasGemmEx (engine\rocm\bin\hipblas.dll)
    #13 strata.exe+0x1899da

**Workaround (confirmed)**
Copying a matching `amdhip64_7.dll` (ROCm 10.2 nightly, 10.0.3686.0) into `engine\` next to `strata.exe` makes Windows load it instead of the System32 copy. The crash is gone and everything works.

Suggested fix: ship the matching `amdhip64_7.dll` next to `strata.exe`, or load it by full path (LoadLibraryExW) at startup before any ROCm library, so the driver's copy can't win.

**Results after the workaround (discrete-card data point)**
- Q2_0, 256K context, 8-bit KV, low-RAM mode: 24,576 experts in VRAM, 100% decode hit rate

issues.title: Windows + 32 GB RAM: the low-RAM resident mode never engages - the fit check runs after the engine's own cache warm-up
issues.author: icocoon
issues.body:
**Version:** Strata 0.1.34 (ready-made `strata-windows-x64-hip.zip` engine), Windows
**OS:** Windows 11 Pro (build 26300), AMD Software: Adrenalin driver 32.0.31035.1003
**GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100)
**CPU:** Ryzen 7 7800X3D (AVX-512) | **RAM:** 32 GB (31.1 GiB usable) | **Disk:** NVMe SSD
**Model:** `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF` IQ2_XS (revision `ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09`), installed by setup itself (`--family qwen --model IQ2_XS`)

## What happens

The low-RAM resident mode (`--resident-experts`, chosen by setup) never engages on this PC; every start falls back to `--mmap-experts` with:

```
strata generate: WARNING: the resident RAM mode does not fit (FileExpertSource: resident complement 16.20 GiB
exceeds available RAM (0.44 GiB) minus the 4 GiB safety headroom); the experts the GPU does not hold are read
from the model folder through the OS file cache (--mmap-experts), which is slower when the RAM cannot keep them
```

`setup.py --check` itself says this configuration fits ("IQ2_XS needs ~48 GB RAM: fits in the low-RAM mode (the GPU holds ~53% of its experts, the rest stays in RAM)"), and MODELS.md states "a 32 GB PC with a 24 GB GPU runs Q2_0, IQ2_XS and the Coder this way".

## Measurements

I probed memory every 2 s from just before starting the server (setup-written config; `STRATA_RESIDENT_PIN=0` as setup wrote it):

```
T-0     available 20.7 GiB                              (clean state, right before start)
T+2s    available 19.9 GiB    strata.exe WS  0.6 GiB
T+10s   available 14.5 GiB    strata.exe WS  5.9 GiB
T+20s   available  7.6 GiB    strata.exe WS 12.7 GiB
T+36s   available  0.5 GiB    strata.exe WS 19.9 GiB
then stable at ~0.5-0.7 GiB
```

The WARNING's position in the engine log shows when the fit check runs - after the engine has fully initialized:

```
strata generate: pre-filled 12551 of 12551 slots from the profile; slot 0 verified
strata generate: R4 hit path ON - resident experts are computed on the GPU
strata generate: 7 expert-pool workers + the host thread
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.34)
strata generate: token graph hit path: 12551 resident experts, decided on the device
strata generate: WARNING: the resident RAM mode does not fit (...)      <-- here
strata serve: prompt chunk auto: 8192 tokens
```

## The math

- Needed for the resident complement: 16.20 GiB + 4 GiB headroom = **20.2 GiB**
- Available in the clean state: **20.7 GiB** - only 0.5 GiB of margin, before any of the engine's own allocations
- Available once the engine has warmed its own caches: **~0.5 GiB**

So the check cannot pass at the moment it runs, and no value of `STRATA_RESIDENT_HEADROOM_GIB` helps (for any headroom >= 0: 0.5 GiB - headroom < 16.2 GiB). On this machine the docs' "32 GB + a 24 GB card runs IQ2_XS in low-RAM mode" is not reachable on Windows.

## Impact

Not a crash: the mmap fallback works (server healthy, correct answers; an informal test measured roughly 47 tok/s including reasoning tokens). But the resident protection against memory pressure is not available - anything that shrinks the OS file cache sends the missing experts back to the SSD - and the documented 32 GB configuration silently degrades.

## Possible fix direction

Read the available memory for the fit check **before** the engine warms its own caches (or reuse the reading taken at the start of initialization), similar in spirit to the #403 fix ("the safety check uses the same RAM reading"). The file-cache pages the engine itself has just created may be counted against available memory here; excluding the engine's own working set from the reading would also fix it.

Related: #403 (a clamped budget fails its own safety check), #250 (miscalculated limits despite theoretically available space), #286 (Windows low-RAM tier).

issues.title: Windows AMD (RX 7900 XTX / gfx1100): prefill GEMM crashes with hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction
issues.author: kopug
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows 11 with an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), Strata 0.1.34 starts successfully, loads the IQ2_XS model, passes `strata-device --selftest`, and can generate responses for short prompts.

However, slightly larger prompts reproducibly crash the engine during prefill with:

```text
rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction':98
prefill gemm: cublasGemmEx: cuBLAS status 6
```

The API then returns HTTP 503:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "server_error",
    "message": "the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code 1); the next request restarts it"
  }
}
```

This does not appear to be specific to long-context / 32K prompts. I originally encountered it while testing a ~32K workload, but was able to reproduce the same crash with much shorter prompts.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 64-bit
- Strata commit: `1678de333d0e0711bc414ad992b640e1a37dd814`
- Strata engine: `0.1.34`
- Backend: HIP
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB
- Architecture: `gfx1100`, wave32
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- RAM: 64 GB DDR5
- AMD display driver: `32.0.31041.1004`
- Driver date reported by Windows: `2026-08-17`
- ROCm libraries shipped with the Windows Strata engine: `10.2.0a20260930`
- Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ2_XS`
- Context: `32768`
- KV: 8-bit
- Vision: disabled

There is also an integrated AMD GPU in the system:

```text
device 0: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics
  arch gfx1036, 36.2 GiB, wave32
  cannot run: GPU 0 (...) is not an architecture this Strata engine was compiled for

device 1: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
  arch gfx1100, 24.0 GiB, wave32
```

Strata setup correctly selects the RX 7900 XTX as HIP device 1.

## Device self-test

I explicitly selected the RX 7900 XTX:

```powershell
$env:HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES = "1"
.\engine\strata-device.exe --selftest
```

Result:

```text
device 0: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
  HIP arch            gfx1100 wave32 (compiled for gfx1100,gfx1101,gfx1102,gfx1200,gfx1201,gfx1030)
  multiprocessors     48
  VRAM total / free   23.984 GiB (25753026560 B) / 23.839 GiB (25596395520 B)
  driver / runtime    70260201 / 70260201

memory plan  --max-context 20480
  KV + indexer keys   0.267387 GB
  recurrent state     0.000000 GB
  expert cache        5.675613 GB
  VRAM pool           5.943000 GB
  expert arena (DRAM) 0.000000 GB
  card free           23.839 GiB (25596395520 B)
  plan + KV vs free   FITS

selftest: arena 0.062 GiB (67108864 B), used 0.002 GiB (2097152 B) after two 1 MiB allocations
selftest: over-allocation refused as required
strata-device selftest OK
```

So basic HIP device detection and the Strata device self-test succeed.

## Successful short inference

A normal short request succeeds:

```text
strata serve: prompt 53 tokens = 0 reused + 53 read in 634 ms (83.6 tok/s), 47 generated in 775 ms (60.6 tok/s), drafts accepted 30 of 32, 1 checkpoints
strata serve: decode expert cache hit rate: 88.5% (19579 hits / 22118 lookups)
```

I also tested exact input-token counts using `/v1/messages/count_tokens`.

Independent short prompts succeeded at approximately 60-62 input tokens:

```text
60 input tokens: OK
61 input tokens: OK
62 input tokens: OK
```

## Reproduction

I generated independent prompts with different prefixes to avoid prefix-cache reuse.

Observed results:

```text
actual input tokens 61 -> OK
actual input tokens 62 -> OK
actual input tokens 61 -> OK
actual input tokens 72 -> HTTP 503 / engine exit
```

The 72-token request causes the engine to terminate.

Earlier tests with larger prompts, including a ~32K workload, fail with the same error.

This suggests the issue is not limited to a full 32K context. It can happen during a relatively short prefill as well.

I did not continue narrowing the exact token boundary because the crash was already reproducible enough to report.

## Engine log at failure

Immediately before the failure:

```text
strata generate: GPU 0: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100)
strata generate: loaded 33.02 GiB at 5.86 GiB/s
strata generate: expert cache auto: 19.19 GiB free, 700 MiB reserved (+143 MiB for the draft head) -> 13053 slots
strata generate: expert cache 13696 slots, 18.36 GiB of VRAM
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.34)
strata generate: token graph hit path: 13696 resident experts, decided on the device
strata serve: prompt chunk auto: 8192 tokens
strata serve: the prompt path borrows 3342 CUDA0 cache slots (4.49 GiB)
strata serve: 477 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded

rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction':98
prefill gemm: cublasGemmEx: cuBLAS status 6
```

The same two error lines appear consistently after the failing requests.

I did not see an out-of-memory error in the engine log.

## Additional observation

The PCIe probe also reports values that appear implausibly high:

```text
PCIe probe: 9038.2 GB/s host->device
PCIe probe: 10294.7 GB/s host->device
PCIe probe: 19416.7 GB/s host->device
PCIe probe: 18417.5 GB/s host->device
PCIe probe: 5598.2 GB/s host->device
```

I do not know whether this is related to the prefill failure, but I included it in case it is useful for debugging.

## Related issues checked

I searched the existing issues before filing this.

The closest one I found is #273:

- RX 7900 XTX / gfx1100 / HIP
- Linux
- engine 0.1.29
- failure in the verify kernel (`unspecified launch failure`)

This report is different:

- Windows 11
- engine 0.1.34
- Windows ready-made HIP engine
- model loading and `strata-device --selftest` succeed
- short inference succeeds
- failure occurs in prefill GEMM
- error is `hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction`

I also found #161, which has a somewhat similar high-level symptom where short prompts succeed and batched prefill fails, but that report is on NVIDIA/CUDA with a different cuBLAS status.

So I do not think this is a duplicate of either issue.

## Expected behavior

Prefill should complete successfully on the RX 7900 XTX / gfx1100 rather than terminating the engine.

## Actual behavior

The engine exits with:

```text
rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction':98
prefill gemm: cublasGemmEx: cuBLAS status 6
```

and the API responds with HTTP 503.

I can provide the full `strata-iq2_xs.log` or run additional targeted diagnostics if useful.

issues.title: Layer split with a small second GPU caps prompt chunk at 512: 6.2x slower prompt reads, same decode
issues.author: DaRealDaHoodie
issues.body:
### Environment

Engine 0.1.31, repo HEAD `9259cad` (2026-10-01). Measured 2026-10-01 on:

- RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell 32 GB (82 SM, CUDA arch 120) + RTX 3080 10 GB (68 SM, arch 86)
- Threadripper PRO 5975WX, 499 GB RAM, Linux
- model `qwen3.8-flash-next-ud-q4_k_xl` (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL split GGUF, 71.73 GiB routed experts
  loaded into the RAM arena), `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp --expert-cache auto`

---
### a small second GPU in a layer split collapses `prompt chunk auto` to 512 tokens (~6x slower prompt reads)

**Symptom.** Same model, same weights, same flags; the only difference is whether the 3080 takes a
slice of the layer split:

| arm | expert cache | `prompt chunk auto` | prompt read | decode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pair (`--layer-split auto`) | CUDA0 8,566 slots + CUDA1 512 slots (1.27 GiB) | **512 tokens** | 127,688 tok in 295,684 ms = **431.8 tok/s** | 85.8 / 86.1 tok/s |
| single stage | CUDA0 7,927 slots | **8192 tokens** | 141,173 tok in 52,955 ms = **2,665.9 tok/s** | 84.8 tok/s |

Decode is unchanged (±1 %). Prompt reads differ by **6.2x**. On an agent workload — long prefixes,
modest generation, most requests re-reading 100-200K tokens — the pair arm is much worse overall,
so the small card's residency gain is not merely neutral, it hides a large prompt regression.

**Cause.** `src/program/generate.cpp:3663-3682`: the chunk is the largest candidate every
participant can fund, and a participant is each stage's own expert cache:

```cpp
auto fits = [&](int64_t c, bool cap) -> bool {
    for (const PfPart& p : pf_parts) {
        const int64_t k = part_slots(p, c);
        if (k <= 0 || k + 128 > p.cache->slots()) return false;
        if (cap && k * 100 > kAutoLendPct * p.cache->slots()) return false;
    }
    return true;
};
```

CUDA1's 512-slot cache must keep the 128-slot floor, so it can fund at most ~384 slots of prompt
staging — the binding constraint for every candidate above 512 tokens. CUDA0's 8,566 slots never
get a say. The comment above `fits()` states the assumption this exposes:

> the chunk is the largest one EVERY participant can lend (a smaller chunk only reads slower)

which is right for comparable cards and wrong when a participant is a small helper card.

Worth stating precisely, because it is easy to misdiagnose: an explicit `--prefill` is **not**
saved by the percentage cap (`fits(c, false)` — the auto scan alone applies `kAutoLendPct`, 85 % or
90 % depending on `Prefill::pinned_share()`). `--prefill 4096` on the pair arm halves down to 512
through the same slot floor and says so:

```
strata serve: prompt chunk 4096 -> 512 tokens so its buffers fit in every expert cache
```

So there is currently no operator setting that keeps a large chunk while the small card is in the
split — the only lever is taking it out of the split, which is a bigger change than tuning.

**Suggested fixes**, roughly in order of how little they disturb the current behaviour:

1. When the candidates are scanned, weight each participant by its share of the loan rather than
   demanding that the smallest cache fund the whole chunk — the large stage can carry most of the
   staging.
2. Or treat a participant whose cache is far below the others (say under 15 % of the largest) as
   unable to lend, letting it stream during the prompt instead of capping everyone.
3. At minimum, name the constraint when the fallback bites, e.g. `prompt chunk auto: 512 tokens
   (CUDA1's 512-slot expert cache cannot fund more)`, so a 6x prompt regression is traceable in one
   log line instead of needing an A/B against a single-card arm. `docs/SECOND_GPU.md` and
   `docs/DETAILS.md` describe split residency and prompt lending separately; neither notes that the
   two interact through this floor.

**Not a bug, for the record:** `--expert-cache-device1` on that same small card is the good use of
it — one stage plus a 1,800-slot tier left `prompt chunk auto: 8192` intact and raised decode from
84.8 to 91.1 tok/s at 167K context (hit rate 69.6 % -> 73.6 %). The tier's own cost is the
per-request synchronisation the docs warn about (`host 74 ms staging+launching, 124 ms waiting for
it`), and it grows with size. 1,800 vs 2,600 slots, requests of similar size:

| tier | hit rate | CUDA1 entries | active layer launches | wait |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,800 | 73.6 % | 6,428 | 2,926 | 124 ms (3.7 % of the request) |
| 2,600 | 78.0 % | 11,061 | 4,491 | 298 ms (6.2 %) |

Residency rose 4.4 points and decode did not (87.7 tok/s at 182K context vs 91.1 at 167K — the
contexts differ, so the wait column is the trustworthy comparison, and it moved 2.4x on 1.5x the
launches). Later, larger requests on the 2,600 tier waited 416-597 ms. The tier has a sweet spot
well below "as much as fits", which is worth a sentence in `docs/SECOND_GPU.md`.

issues.title: --calibrate silently leaves the machine uncalibrated when the config uses --expert-cache-deviceN
issues.author: DaRealDaHoodie
issues.body:
### Environment

Engine 0.1.31, repo HEAD `9259cad` (2026-10-01). Measured 2026-10-01 on:

- RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell 32 GB (82 SM, CUDA arch 120) + RTX 3080 10 GB (68 SM, arch 86)
- Threadripper PRO 5975WX, 499 GB RAM, Linux
- model `qwen3.8-flash-next-ud-q4_k_xl` (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL split GGUF, 71.73 GiB routed experts
  loaded into the RAM arena), `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --spec 4 --mtp --expert-cache auto`

---
### `--calibrate` cannot calibrate a config that uses the helper-GPU expert tier

**Symptom.** `./setup.sh --calibrate` on a config that uses `--expert-cache-device1` prints one
warning and then starts the model as if nothing happened:

```
  Loading the model for the measurements ...
[strata] starting the engine: reading the model's weights ...
  [!]  the tuning did not finish (the engine exited before it was ready (see strata-ud-q4_k_xl.log)): the default settings stay
  [ok] GPUs: GPU 0 (NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell, 32 GB) together (layers split auto)
```

No calibration record is written, the config keeps its old flags, and a user who is not watching
the two lines above has an uncalibrated machine and no way to know it.

**Cause.** `tools/calibrate.py:123` reads "the config has a `gpu` list" as "this model splits
layers across several cards":

```python
if isinstance(cfg.get("gpu"), list) and "--layer-split" not in args:   # several cards: measured as it runs
    args += ["--layer-split", str(cfg.get("layer_split") or "auto")]
```

A `gpu` list does not imply a split. `serve/server.py:engine_args()` uses the correct test
(`len(gpu_list(cfg)) > 1`), and the helper-tier feature documented in `docs/SECOND_GPU.md` works
the other way round: the tier needs a card that runs **no** stage, so the config is one stage plus
a second *visible* card:

```json
"gpu": [0],
"env": { "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "0,1" },
"args": [ ..., "--expert-cache-device1", "1800" ]
```

The tuner's appended `--layer-split auto` puts both visible cards into stages, and the engine
rejects that combination before reading any weights (`src/program/generate.cpp`):

```
strata generate: --expert-cache-remote with a layer split needs a GPU that runs no stage (2 visible, 2 used by the split)
```

**Amplifier.** `setup.py:1663-1667` turns that into a single `!` line and continues, by design
("never stops an install"). Given that the whole point of the step is to leave the machine tuned,
it is worth printing the engine's own error (it is in the log, one line above the next start) or
repeating the warning in the `All set.` summary.

**Suggested fix.** Mirror `engine_args()`:

```python
if len(gpu_list(cfg)) > 1 and "--layer-split" not in args:
```

**Workaround** (no source change, and it also documents the intent in the config): pass the split
as empty, which is the engine's "no split" value — the parse block is gated on
`if (!o.layer_split.empty())` (`src/program/generate.cpp:1232`), and `--layer-split none` is
rejected while `--layer-split ""` parses and moves on:

```json
"args": [ ..., "--layer-split", "" ]
```

**Evidence.** Same command, before and after the workaround — model loads recorded in the config's
log (opened in append mode, `serve/server.py:173`), so a sweep that never started an engine leaves
no loads:

| | loads / serve starts in log | record written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--calibrate`, before | 2 (both from ordinary starts) | none |
| `--calibrate`, after | 7 (the sweep ran) | `…\|32GB\|…qwen3.8-flash-next-ud-q4_k_xl\|262144\|text` |

The sweep then chose `--pcie-frac 0.00 --spec-min-p 0.70` (102.4 tok/s), which is the result this
report is about: with the tier present the tuner can now measure the topology that actually runs.

issues.title: setup (--backend hip): a runtime-only system ROCm 7 in /opt/rocm is picked for the engine build, and cmake fails on the missing hip-lang package instead of falling back to the TheRock wheels
issues.author: harurun78
issues.body:
### What happens

`./setup.sh --backend hip` on a PC whose `/opt/rocm` has the ROCm 7.14 runtime packages but not the development ones stops in step 4:

```
  The ROCm root directory:

   /opt/rocm

  does not contain the HIP runtime CMake package, expected at one of:

   /opt/rocm/lib/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake
   /opt/rocm/lib64/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake
   /opt/rocm/lib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake

Call Stack (most recent call first):
  cmake/hip_backend.cmake:38 (enable_language)
  CMakeLists.txt:50 (include)

-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!

  [X]  command failed (exit 1): cmake
```

### Why

`rocm_root()` in setup.py takes the system ROCm when `bin/hipcc` and `lib/libhipblas.so*` exist and the version is 7.0 or newer. A runtime-only install has both, so the check passes:

- `/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc` exists (on this install it comes from `amdrocm-llvm7.14`)
- `/opt/rocm/lib/libhipblas.so*` and `libamdhip64.so*` exist
- `include/rocm-core/rocm_version.h` says 7.14

The parts the build needs are missing, though: `lib/cmake/hip-lang/`, `lib/cmake/hip/` and `include/hip/hip_runtime.h`. On AMD's 26.13 repo the HIP ones ship in `amdrocm-runtime-dev7.14` (checked with `dpkg -c`), which, like `amdrocm-blas-dev7.14`, comes with `amdrocm-core-dev7.14-gfx1201`; none of the `-dev` packages are installed here. So setup never tries the TheRock wheels path, which works on this PC without sudo.

### Workaround

Point `ROCM_PATH` somewhere without ROCm, so setup takes the TheRock wheels path:

```sh
ROCM_PATH=$HOME/.no-system-rocm ./setup.sh --backend hip
```

With that, the setup ran to the end (ROCm 7.10.0a20251120 wheels from `gfx120X-all`, engine compiled, IQ3_XXS ready), and the server answers normally, tool calls included.

### Suggested fix

Have the system-ROCm check also look for the files the build needs (for example `lib/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake` and `include/hip/hip_runtime.h`). When they are missing, warn and use the wheels, the same way an older ROCm is handled now:

```
[!] the ROCm in /opt/rocm has no HIP development files (lib/cmake/hip-lang): using AMD's wheels in .venv instead
    (or install them, e.g. sudo apt install amdrocm-core-dev7.14-gfx1201)
```

(I have not tried the build with the `-dev` packages installed; the wheels path is the one verified here.)

Note: open PR #426 (Windows AMD) also changes `rocm_root()`, so this fix may be easier on top of it.

### Environment

- Strata `main` @ aeb35be (the code in question is the same on 1678de3)
- Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic
- AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB (gfx1201), Ryzen 9 3950X, 63 GB RAM
- amdgpu-install 31.40 + AMD's repo `rocmradeon/apt/26.13`: `amdrocm-*7.14` 7.14.0~pre3 runtime packages (`amdrocm-core7.14-gfx1201`, `amdrocm-blas7.14-gfx1201`, `amdrocm-llvm7.14`, ...), no `-dev` packages
- Command: `./setup.sh --backend hip --yes --no-start`

issues.title: Large arena prefill regression on Linux: 42-43 GiB pin threshold stalls GPU
issues.author: mohammedalsayegh
issues.body:
Greetings! 

first, thanks for the great work!

Found a performance regression testing on multiple P100s (sm_60 / Pascal). Unclear if Pascal-specific or affects newer architectures.

Commit `ed6c124` ("#253: the 8 GiB arena pin cap only under WDDM") causes large expert arenas to lose most prompt speed on Linux. The environment variable from that commit recovers performance, so this likely needs a different default or release note.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **IQ3_S** (`arena_gb` 50.3) |
| GPUs | 3 × Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB (sm_60) |
| Topology | GPU0 in PCIe x4, GPU1/2 in x16 — auto layer split |
| RAM | 125 GB |
| CPU | Xeon E5-2699 v3 (AVX2 only) |
| CUDA / driver | 12.0 / 580.178.04 |
| Engine | `-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=60` |

### Key Triggers
- **Arena Size:** Performance cliff at ~84% of arena size. Smaller CI arenas won't reproduce this.
- **Layer Split:** Required condition per `ed6c124`.
- **RAM Headroom:** Available RAM stays 67-68 GB — this is a threshold issue, not exhaustion.
- **Architecture:** sm_60 without AVX-512. GPU arch might matter; CPU likely doesn't.

## Results

Median of ≥2 rounds, fresh ~7.3K-token prompts (cached prompts ~0.45s, not measured).

| build | `STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB` | prefill tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| `30ec18e` (v0.1.30) | — | **179.7** |
| `ed6c124` (first bad) | — | 134.6 |
| `c499bd1` (v0.1.32) | — | 133.5 |
| `aeb35be` (v0.1.33) | — | 127.0 |
| **`aeb35be`, unmodified** | **40** | **192.2** |

Same pattern at 69,144 tokens: 125.0 → 204.3 tok/s. Gap widens at larger prompts.

## Why this matters

#253 was resolved but didn't fix this for my setup. With layer split, default pins entire arena (past 42-43 GiB cliff): 127 tok/s default vs 192 tok/s with undocumented variable. Severely hinders large-context performance. Unclear if this affects single-GPU or only multi-GPU, but #253's fix clearly didn't cover all cases.

## Discrete Performance Threshold

| `STRATA_ARENA_PIN_GIB` | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 40 | 41 | 42 | **43** | 44 | unset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| prefill | 177.8 | 179.6 | 183.3 | 184.2 | **192.2** | fast | fast | **slow** | 134.0 | 127.0 |
| prompt loan | 1.49 | 1.49 | 1.49 | 1.49 | **1.49** | 1.49 | 1.49 | **0.68** | 0.68 | 0.68 |

Degradation is discrete (loan halves between 42-43 GiB), consistent across 7.3K and 69K tokens. RAM stable at 67-68 GB confirms threshold logic issue.

`STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1` shows 96.5% loss in `embed+steps` ("gap where GPU waits" per `prefill.cpp` comments) — GPU stalls on host expert feed, not slower kernels. These env vars didn't help: `STRATA_OLD_GROUPED=1`, `STRATA_REFILL_SERIAL=1`, `STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=4`, `STRATA_SPLIT_OWN=0`, `STRATA_PREFILL_AUTO_MAX=8192`, `STRATA_PREFILL_LEND_PCT` (60-90).

## Where to Look

Loan halves at 83-85% arena pinned. `generate.cpp` has `pinned_share() >= 0.9 ? 90 : 85` threshold. Values are close but `STRATA_PREFILL_LEND_PCT` didn't affect loan, so likely different thresholds. Coupling between arena pin % and prompt loan logic is probably there.

issues.title: CJK output is systematically wrong at IQ1_M: 0/10 correct on Chinese, 10/10 on English (greedy)
issues.author: lybhb8
issues.body:
**Affected:** Engine 0.1.30 (`2a57d8d`), native i-quant expert packs, HIP/gfx1100 build
(ROCm 10.0). Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ1_M` (the `Coder` GGUF, IQ1_M = 1-bit).
Reported against the Coder repo's only published quant.

At temperature 0, Chinese output is **never** correct on this box. It either degrades into a
single-token loop or drops a character. English is unaffected. This is reproducible on every
run and is not a sampling artifact.

### Reproduction

Server: `serve.server --engine strata` with the standard Coder config
(`--expert-cache auto --mmap-experts --mtp rt --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --prefill auto
--max-context 65536 --kv int8 --vision`), reasoning off.

Prompt: `用一句话说明你是哪个模型，跑在什么硬件上。`

Two distinct failure modes, both wrong:

    我是通（通通通通通通通通通通通通通通…      finish_reason=length   ← degenerate, single-token loop
    我是通千（Qwen），由阿里巴巴通千团队开发     ← no loop, but 「通义千问」 lost the 「义」

The second one is the more informative case: the answer is *structurally* correct and the
model clearly wants to say 通义千问, but it emits 通千. The character 义 is not merely
misordered — it is absent.

### Quantified

Same prompt, `temperature: 0`, `reasoning_effort: none`, n=10 per language:

| language | correct | wrong-but-fluent | degenerate loop |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| English (equivalent question) | **10** | 0 | 0 |
| Chinese | **0** | 5 | 5 |

English answers are byte-identical across all 10 runs. Chinese is 0-for-10 correct.

### What I ruled out (each by ablation, not by reasoning)

| variable | experiment | result |
|---|---|---|
| suffix (prompt-lookup) drafter | `--suffix-draft 0` | still degenerates |
| verify window width | `--spec 2` vs `4` | still degenerates |
| speculative accept path | engine reports 63/71 and 48/48 drafts accepted | accept logic is correct — it only commits tokens the target verified (`generate.cpp:4761`) |
| GPU vs CPU expert rounding | `--expert-cache` 1500 → 9019 slots (hit 62% → 97%) | degenerates at every size |
| KV quantization | `--kv fp16`, `--kv k8v4`, full-VRAM config | still degenerates |
| sampling | `temperature: 0` (greedy) | still degenerates |
| repetition penalties | `penalty_repeat` 1.15/1.2, `penalty_freq`, `penalty_present`, with `penalty_last_n` 64/256 | no effect; does not escape even at 300 tokens |
| draft-independence switch | `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` (which 0.1.30 setup now requires, #152) | 5/5 still degenerate |
| run-to-run variance | 6 consecutive identical greedy requests | 6/6 degenerate (stable) |

**A caution about single-sample conclusions:** one `--kv fp16` run came back clean and looked
like the root cause. Re-running that exact config gave 3 clean / 1 degenerate over 4 runs, then
5 wrong / 5 degenerate over 10. The clean run was luck. fp16 only shifts the failure mix; it
fixes nothing.

### Observations that may be relevant

1. **The failure is CJK-specific.** English is unaffected, which argues against a general
   numerical problem.
2. **The pack's `vocab.json` contains no merged CJK tokens at all** — `通`, `千`, `义` are not
   keys in the 248,320-entry vocab, and zero entries contain a CJK character. There are 66,744
   byte-fallback entries. CJK is byte-mapped, consistent with #268's finding that the
   tokenizer byte-maps each CJK character to 1–3 byte-chars.
3. **IQ1_M is 1-bit** (`vec_dot_iq1_m_q8_1`, `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu:223`). Combined
   with (2), a Han character costs 3 tokens of a 1-bit budget, versus 1 token for an English
   word — plausibly a large effective precision deficit exactly where the failures land.
4. **`draft_vocab.bin` is absent from `mtp/rt/`** on this install (only `dense.bin`,
   `dense.txt`, `experts.bin`), and this build's `--help` has no `--draft-vocab` option, so the
   CJK draft subset described in `docs/DETAILS.md:82` is not present here. Per #137 a *missing*
   `draft_vocab.bin` means the full native head, which was measured as **faster**, so I do not
   think this causes the quality failure — but it means the documented CJK drafting path does
   not exist in this build.

### Why this was not caught by the test suite

`grep -rlP '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]' bench/ tests/` returns **nothing** — no file under `bench/` or
`tests/` contains a Chinese character. Every quality result in the repo rests on English or
synthetic prompts.

Related: `bench/results/2026-09-27-kv-q4/README.md` concludes "int8 is indistinguishable from
fp16" from mean KL and perplexity on English code/document/chat text. A mean-based metric
cannot catch this class of failure: the flip happens at one near-tied token, the mean barely
moves, but greedy decoding locks in permanently.

### Questions

1. Is a 1-bit quant expected to support CJK at all, or is IQ1_M intended as English/code-only?
   `docs/DETAILS.md` advertises CJK draft-vocab support for 15–38% faster CJK answers, which
   implies CJK is meant to work.
2. Is there a known-good (non-1-bit) configuration on this model that produces correct Chinese?
   The `Coder` HF repo publishes only IQ1_M; IQ3_XXS / Q2_0 exist in the separate
   `…-GSQ-RCO-GGUF` repo, which is a different fine-tune, so I could not run a clean
   quant-only ablation.
3. Would a CJK prompt set in `bench/` (even a small one) be accepted? It looks like the gap
   that let this through.

### Environment

- RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), ROCm 10.0, engine built locally with hipcc
- Xeon E5-2696 v4 (AVX2, no AVX-512), 62 GB RAM
- Engine 0.1.30, commit `2a57d8d`

### Related / not the same as

#137 (missing `draft_vocab.bin` collapses CJK *draft acceptance* — a speed issue; a *missing* file means
the full native head, measured faster there) and #268 (tokenizer byte-maps CJK 3x, consistent with (2)
above). #152 is closed and covers CPU expert arithmetic varying with verifier width: with
`STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` on, and at `--spec 2`, and across every expert-cache size, CJK output is still wrong
5/5 — so I do not think #152 is the cause.

issues.title: Benchmark report: R9700 (gfx1201) on 0.1.32 with TheRock 7.10 — router +12% not reproduced, HIP_WMMA prompt +29-34%
issues.author: jkuepker
issues.body:
This is a report of numbers measured against the release-note claims, not a bug report. All runs used the same Coder IQ1_M pack on one R9700. localeval streamed sweeps: fresh nonce each call (no prefix cache), 128 forced output tokens, temperature 0, median of reps after a warmup. The server was restarted for every configuration.

| Config | Prompt 4K (tok/s) | Prompt 16K (tok/s) | Decode 128 / 1K / 4K (tok/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| default | 1,331 | 1,310 | 91.0 / 75.3 / 68.0 |
| `STRATA_HIP_ROUTER_OLD=1` | 1,215 | 1,312 | 81.7 / 69.6 / 68.7 |
| `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1` | **1,712 (+29%)** | **1,759 (+34%)** | 85.2 / 70.0 / 68.8 |
| `STRATA_SELECT_WMMA=1` | 1,223 | 1,324 (+1%) | 88.7 / 70.2 / 65.3 |
| `--pool-affinity auto` (12600K P/E cores) | 1,336 | 1,314 | 82.9 / 74.3 / 64.2 |

**Router A/B/A/B rerun (6 reps each, decode tok/s):**

| Run | 128 | 1K | 4K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| new | 91.9 | 71.2 | 63.3 |
| old | 90.7 | 70.5 | 66.3 |
| new | 90.6 | 74.5 | 68.1 |
| old | 89.4 | 69.7 | 62.8 |

- **Router:** the new router averages +1-4% decode. The spread within a run is 12-20%, so I can't detect the +12% (62 → 70 tok/s) the notes report. I confirmed the engine received `STRATA_HIP_ROUTER_OLD=1` by reading `/proc/<pid>/environ`. Greedy output is bit-identical between the two routers across 10 server starts, which matches the notes.
- **HIP_WMMA:** a clear gain, but below the +36-51% in the notes. The greedy 256-token output hash did not change on a short prompt.
- **SELECT_WMMA:** +1% at 16K, in line with the +1.5% in the notes.
- **A difference that may matter:** the release numbers came from ROCm 10.2 nightly with hipBLASLt 1.5.0. This box uses what setup installs, TheRock 7.10 wheels with hipBLASLt 1.2.0, so the shipped gfx1201 tuning table doesn't load. Another difference is the CPU: an i5-12600K here, versus 16 threads on the author's machine.

Question: what prompt length and which settings produced the 62 → 70 tok/s figure? With those I can rerun under the same conditions.

issues.title: Cancelling a streaming request during a long prompt read only takes effect after the full prompt is read
issues.author: jkuepker
issues.body:
With `"stream": true`, a disconnect is detected (`cancel=True`, 0 tokens generated), but only after the whole prompt has been read. On a 57K-token prompt, the next request waited about 17 s.

**Repro:**
1. Stream a 57,396-token request and disconnect after 6 s:
   ```bash
   curl -s -N -m 6 127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @long-57k-stream.json
   ```
2. Immediately send "Say OK." (max_tokens 30).

**Observed:**
```
strata serve: prompt 57396 tokens = 0 reused + 57396 read in 22151 ms (2591.2 tok/s), 0 generated ..., 2 checkpoints (cancelled)
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 22 s (0.0 tok/s) (disconnect, cancel=True)
```
The follow-up request took **17.2 s**, even though it only needed about 0.9 s of engine time.

`serve/server.py` already checks `cancel` on every `PP` progress line. So either the engine doesn't act on STOP between prefill chunks, or `--prefill auto` makes the chunks so large that the first check comes late. I haven't checked which.

**Expected:** a cancel during the prompt read stops it at the next chunk boundary.

The release notes for 0.1.32 list "a cancelled long prompt followed by a new request" as checked. That claim holds: the new request is answered correctly with no engine restart. This issue is only about how long the new request waits.

**Environment**

```
Strata v0.1.32 (tag c499bd1), Linux, Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 7.0.0-34
GPU: Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201), single card
CPU: i5-12600K (AVX2, no AVX-512), 62 GB DDR5
Setup: ./setup.sh --backend hip --family coder --model IQ1_M (no system ROCm)
ROCm: TheRock 7.10.0a20251120 wheels (gfx120X-all) installed by setup into .venv; hipBLASLt 1.2.0
Server: serve/server.py with setup's generated config (max-context 131072, kv int8, spec 4 + MTP)
```

issues.title: serve: non-streaming request is not cancelled when the client disconnects; the engine runs to max_tokens and blocks the next request
issues.author: jkuepker
issues.body:
When a client drops a non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` request (for example, a timeout), the engine keeps going. It reads the whole prompt and generates up to `max_tokens`. The next request waits for all of that to finish.

**Repro:**
1. Send a long non-streaming request and drop it after 4 s:
   ```bash
   curl -s -m 4 127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @long-57k.json   # max_tokens 300
   ```
2. Immediately send a small request ("Say OK.", max_tokens 30).

**Observed:** the engine log shows the dropped request ran to the end (41,012 tokens read in 30.6 s, then all 300 tokens generated). The small request took **33 s**.
```
strata serve: prompt 57396 tokens = 16384 reused + 41012 read in 30626 ms (1339.1 tok/s), 300 generated in 4673 ms (64.2 tok/s) ...
```

**Expected:** the request is cancelled soon after the disconnect, as streaming requests already are (`finish = "disconnect"`). One possible approach: while a non-streaming request runs, poll the client socket for EOF, for example with `select` and `MSG_PEEK` on each heartbeat or `PP` line, and set `cancel` when it closes.

This matters for clients with request timeouts, such as agents and proxies. A timed-out request keeps occupying the single engine.

**Environment**

```
Strata v0.1.32 (tag c499bd1), Linux, Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 7.0.0-34
GPU: Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201), single card
CPU: i5-12600K (AVX2, no AVX-512), 62 GB DDR5
Setup: ./setup.sh --backend hip --family coder --model IQ1_M (no system ROCm)
ROCm: TheRock 7.10.0a20251120 wheels (gfx120X-all) installed by setup into .venv; hipBLASLt 1.2.0
Server: serve/server.py with setup's generated config (max-context 131072, kv int8, spec 4 + MTP)
```

issues.title: setup: UD-Q4_K_XL is offered (and not blocked) on --backend hip, though docs/UNSLOTH_Q4.md says it needs an NVIDIA GPU

On an AMD-only PC, `./setup.sh --check --backend hip` lists the experimental Unsloth model as fitting:

```
UD-Q4_K_XL needs ~48 GB RAM: EXPERIMENTAL, fits with 38 GiB of its experts in RAM, the rest read from the SSD
```

`docs/UNSLOTH_Q4.md` says it needs "48 GB of RAM or more and engine 0.1.32 or newer ... and an NVIDIA GPU."

Reading `setup.py` at v0.1.32: the UD-Q4_K_XL checks before the download cover the RAM size (`MODELS[model]["ram_gb"]`) and the engine version (`UNSLOTH_ENGINE`), but nothing checks the backend. So an AMD user can pick it and start the 111 GB download. I did not try the download, so I don't know whether the HIP engine actually runs it (`--compat-bf16`, resident-budget mode).

**Expected:** one of these:
- If HIP isn't supported: `--check` marks UD-Q4_K_XL as "NVIDIA only" when the backend is hip, and setup refuses it before downloading. This matches how the RAM and engine-version checks run first.
- If HIP is meant to work: update `docs/UNSLOTH_Q4.md` and say it is untested on AMD.

issues.title: 0.1.32 aborts with mmq.cuh:1555 fatal error (J_best=0) on a 77-token prompt, SM 12.0, 2 GPUs, Swift IQ3_XXS
issues.author: qni-live
issues.body:
Engine 0.1.32 aborts on the first longer request. Engine 0.1.30 with the same settings, model and pack runs fine.

Setup
- 2x RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (SM 12.0, 32 GB each), driver 595.84, CUDA 13.3 toolkit, Ubuntu 26.04
- Engine built from the v0.1.32 source tarball with `setup.py --build` (arch 120, source built on this PC, not the ready-made engine)
- Model: Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS pack, `--layer-split 25`, `--kv k8v4`, `--spec 5 --spec-min-p 0.5`, MTP, `--prefill auto`, vision on
- Same config file as the 0.1.30 run that works (only `exe` points at the 0.1.32 build)

What happens
- Server starts and prints `ready`.
- First request: a chat completion with a 77-token prompt (`max_tokens 256`, temperature 0).
- The server prints `reading the prompt: 77 tokens, 10 s so far`, then the engine aborts:

```
J_best=0
.../third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/template-instances/../mmq.cuh:1555: fatal error
```

- Happened in 2 of 2 runs with that request.
- Three much shorter requests ("Say hi. 1/2/3", about 20 tokens, `max_tokens 20`) in the same setup did answer, also with `--prefill 512` and with `--spec 4`. I did not find the exact prompt length where it starts, and I did not test other models or one GPU.

Not tested: whether it is my local build or the release code; whether one GPU or another quantization shows it.

Logs available: server log with the abort, the config file. I can try a given length or flag if you tell me what is useful.

issues.title: strata-vision.exe v0.1.32 prebuilt crashes (0xC000001D) on CPUs without AVX-512: unguarded AVX-512 vmovups at strata_vision+0x285545
issues.author: lxfebd
issues.body:
## Summary

The prebuilt `strata-vision.exe` shipped in the v0.1.32 release crashes with `STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` (0xC000001D) on any CPU without AVX-512. A debugger shows the faulting instruction is an **EVEX-encoded `vmovups zmm0` inside strata-vision.exe itself**, executed during startup with no CPUID runtime dispatch. The main engine binary from the same release is fine — it correctly falls back (`this CPU has no AVX-512: the expert kernels run on AVX-2`) — and the v0.1.27 `strata-vision.exe` works on the same machine and model files.

This affects a large installed base: every Intel consumer chip 12th–14th gen (AVX-512 fused-disabled) and AMD Zen 4 has no AVX-512. The release advertises `"portable": true` in BUILD.json, so the runtime dispatch is expected to cover this.

## Environment

- Windows 11 10.0.26200, i7-13700KF (AVX2/FMA only, no AVX-512), RTX 5090D 24 GB
- Engine: official prebuilt v0.1.32 release, `BUILD.json`: `{"version": "0.1.32", "source": "release", "cuda": "13.0", "vision": "gpu", "portable": true, "vision_archs": [75, 86, 89, 120], "ptx": true}`
- `strata-vision.exe` = 107,928,064 bytes, sha256 begins `bd5bd917c4d34849…`
- (v0.1.27 `strata-vision.exe` = 90,725,376 bytes, sha256 begins `98ffde98f5388b51…`, works fine)

## Reproduce

```bat
strata-vision.exe --mmproj <mmproj gguf> --model <model gguf> --gpu
```

- No args: usage prints fine, exits 2 (so the binary loads; the crash is during model/backend init).
- With args: exits immediately, code `0xC000001D`, **empty stderr, no READY line**. The v0.1.27 binary prints `READY 2560` in ~6 s with the same files.
- `--flash-attn off` → same crash, so it is not the new #288 flash-attn path.
- Omitting `--gpu` → `ggml_cuda_init: failed to initialize CUDA …` is printed (CUDA deliberately unavailable), then the **same crash on the pure-CPU path** — so it is a host-code issue, not a GPU kernel issue.
- Same crash when launched from the server with the server's own child env, and from a plain console: unrelated to how it is spawned.

## Crash evidence (WinDbg `cdb.exe`)

```
(9b8c.90cc): Illegal instruction - code c000001d (!!! second chance !!!)
strata_vision+0x285545:
00007ff7`1c405545 62f17c4810052114c200 vmovups zmm0,zmmword ptr [strata_vision+0xea6970]
Child-SP          RetAddr               Call Site
00000079`f737f510 00007ff7`1c23a9e3     strata_vision+0x285545
00000079`f737f540 00007ff7`1c249ec9     strata_vision+0xba9e3
00000079`f737f600 00007ff7`1c1e1cc4     strata_vision+0xc9ec9
00000079`f737f710 00007ff7`1c1eadd2     strata_vision+0x61cc4
00000079`f737f880 00007ff7`1c1dd9f1     strata_vision+0x6add2
00000079`f737f8d0 00007ff7`1cfe750c     strata_vision+0x5d9f1
00000079`f737fc90 00007ffe`a994cd87     strata_vision+0xe6750c   (thread start)
00000079`f737fcd0 00007ffe`aaaacaec     KERNEL32!BaseThreadInitThunk+0x17
```

`62 …` = EVEX prefix, `zmm0` = 512-bit register: an AVX-512 instruction reached unconditionally during startup on a non-AVX-512 CPU. Whatever introduced it between 0.1.27 and 0.1.32 vision builds was compiled without runtime dispatch (e.g. a `/arch:AVX512` TU or an AVX-512 intrinsic constant-load in an init path).

## Impact / workaround in use

Vision is completely unavailable on non-AVX-512 CPUs with the 0.1.32 prebuilt (`RuntimeError: the vision encoder did not start:`). We pinned the 0.1.27 `strata-vision.exe` next to the 0.1.32 engine as a workaround and it works end-to-end (image requests answered via `/v1/messages`).

Suggest: add a CPUID guard (or build the vision exe with the same dispatch policy as the main engine), and maybe a CI smoke run on a non-AVX-512 runner.

issues.title: test_setup_choices fails on a host with a real CUDA install: find_nvcc()'s /usr/local/cuda* glob is not mocked
issues.author: rwkeyes
issues.body:
**What happens.** `tools/test_setup_choices.py::ExperimentalSm60.test_find_nvcc_below` errors on any machine that has a CUDA toolkit installed:

```
ERROR: test_find_nvcc_below (test_setup_choices.ExperimentalSm60)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tools/test_setup_choices.py", line 132, in test_find_nvcc_below
    self.assertEqual(setup.find_nvcc(), (str(new), (13, 0)))
  File "setup.py", line 604, in find_nvcc
    v = re.search(r"release (\d+)\.(\d+)", out([c, "--version"]))
  File "tools/test_setup_choices.py", line 131, in <lambda>
    mock.patch.object(setup, "out", lambda cmd: versions[cmd[0]]):
KeyError: '/usr/local/cuda-13.2/bin/nvcc'
```

Reproduced on two hosts, each failing on **its own** toolkit path — CUDA 13.2 at `/usr/local/cuda-13.2` (plus `/usr/bin/nvcc`), and CUDA 12.8 at `/usr/local/cuda-12.8`:

```
KeyError: '/usr/local/cuda-12.8/bin/nvcc'
```

Seen from `python -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'` on 0.1.32 (`c499bd1`), on both a HIP/gfx1100 box and a CUDA 12.8 box.

**Why.** The test mocks `WIN`, `shutil.which`, `CUDA_PATH` and `setup.out`, but `find_nvcc()` also enumerates the *real* filesystem:

```python
cands += [str(p / "bin" / "nvcc") for p in sorted(Path("/usr/local").glob("cuda*"), reverse=True)]
cands += [str(p / "bin" / "nvcc") for p in sorted(Path("/opt").glob("cuda*"), reverse=True)]   # Arch (#46)
```

Those real candidates are appended to the mocked ones. They are normally **newer** than the test's fake `13.0`, so they win the loop, and the mocked `out()` has no entry for them → `KeyError`.

**Confirmation.** Faking the glob out — returning nothing for `cuda*` — makes the test pass unchanged:

```python
real = pathlib.Path.glob
pathlib.Path.glob = lambda self, pat, **k: iter(()) if "cuda" in str(pat) else real(self, pat, **k)
# -> failures=0 errors=0
```

So the cause is the unmocked glob and nothing about the host.

**Suggested fix.** Mock the cuda-root enumeration as well (`mock.patch.object(Path, "glob", ...)`), or make the roots injectable so the test can point `find_nvcc()` at its temp directory.

**This is not a product bug** — `find_nvcc()` does exactly what it should, and the engine/setup path is unaffected. It is test hermeticity only, and it is invisible on a machine without CUDA installed, which is presumably why CI does not catch it.

issues.title: 0.1.32 ready-made strata-vision.exe crashes with illegal instruction (0xC000001D) on a non-AVX-512 CPU (i9-9900KF)
issues.author: Efs-O
issues.body:
**Summary:** after updating to the 0.1.32 ready-made engine (`strata-windows-x64.zip`), `strata-vision.exe` dies at startup with `0xC000001D` (STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION). The process prints nothing and exits, so `serve/server.py` stops with `RuntimeError: the vision encoder did not start:` and the empty line it read. `strata.exe` from the same zip runs fine on the same PC: the model serves text on 0.1.32. The 0.1.30 `strata-vision.exe` ran on this machine without problems.

**PC**
- CPU: Intel i9-9900KF (Coffee Lake: AVX2, **no AVX-512**)
- GPUs: 2x RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (sm_120) running the model as a layer split, plus an RTX 3060 12 GB (sm_86)
- Windows 10 Pro 19045
- `engine/BUILD.json`: `"version": "0.1.32", "source": "release", "archs": [75, 86, 89, 120], "vision": "gpu", "portable": true`

**Repro:** run the encoder directly, outside the server:
```
strata-vision.exe --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-BF16.gguf --model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf --gpu
```
- with `--gpu` and every GPU visible: exit `0xC000001D`, no output
- with `--gpu` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` set to one card: same
- without `--gpu` (CPU): it prints `ggml_cuda_init: failed to initialize CUDA: no CUDA-capable device is detected`, then exits `0xC000001D`

The same happens under the server's own environment (`child_env`, PATH with the `nvidia/cu13` wheel bin): exit code `3221225501`.

**Guess:** the CPU-side ggml in the 0.1.32 vision build was compiled with AVX-512 (or `GGML_NATIVE` on the build machine) instead of the portable baseline the 0.1.30 build used. Running `strata-vision.exe --help` exits normally, so it seems to fail on the first ggml CPU code path, not at load.

**Workaround for now:** vision is turned off in the config, and the engine itself runs on 0.1.32. Thanks for #340, by the way: a ~7.5K-token prompt went from ~30 s to 10.4 s on our two 5060 Tis.

issues.title: Greedy output varies between server requests, but not between fresh engine runs (`STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`, 0.1.32)
issues.author: brenoperucchi
issues.body:
Follow-up to #152. With `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`, temperature 0 still gives different answers to identical requests on
this machine. The engine itself looks deterministic: the variation comes from state the server carries from one
request to the next, and the adaptive expert tier explains at least part of it.

**Machine:** RTX 5090 32 GB, Ryzen 9 5950X (Zen 3, AVX2 only), 96 GB DDR4-3200, Windows 11 26200.
**Engine:** 0.1.32 from the release zip, with the `v0.1.32` checkout's `serve/server.py`.
**Model and config:** Flash-Next IQ2_XS with `--expert-cache auto --spec 4 --mtp <rt> --max-context 32768 --kv int8
--pcie-frac 0.55 --spec-min-p 0.70` and `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`.
**Requests:** `/v1/chat/completions`, `temperature 0`, `seed 42`, `cache_prompt false`, `max_tokens 256`, one after
another on one server. We compare the SHA-256 of the returned content.

## Results

| Setup | Prompt | Distinct outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Engine CLI, a new process each run, `--tokens` (41 fixed ids) `--max-new 64` | short | 1 of 5; the `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS` file is identical too |
| Server, defaults | short (27 tokens) | 2 of 5 |
| Server, `--prompt-cache 0` | short | 3 of 6 |
| Server, `--prompt-cache 0 --adapt-swaps 0` | short | 1 of 6, with the same draft acceptance every time |
| same | medium (2,671 tokens) | 3 of 4 |
| Server, `--prompt-cache 0 --adapt-swaps 0 --no-prefill-borrow` | medium | 4 of 4 |
| same | long (5,952 tokens) | 1 of 4 |

With the defaults, draft acceptance on the short prompt moved between 36 and 37 of 48-49 across requests even when
the text came out the same.

On 0.1.31 we had already ruled out the GPU/CPU split by itself: with `--expert-cache 1 --pcie-frac 0` (decode cache
hit rate 0.1%) outputs still varied, 2 to 3 distinct in 5. The adaptive tier was on in that run.

## What we think is going on

The adaptive tier moves experts between RAM and VRAM based on what earlier requests routed. The GPU and the CPU round
the same expert differently (the startup message says so), so the same token can be computed on a different device
from one request to the next. Turning the tier off made the short prompt reproducible.

We cannot explain the medium prompt yet. It still varies with the tier off and with `--no-prefill-borrow`, while the
longer prompt does not. Something else that persists between requests seems to affect the prompt path at that length.

We are not reporting a quality problem. Greedy repeats are not byte-identical, which gets in the way of A/B tests.
The docs say `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1` makes the answer independent of the drafting. It may help to add that the
adaptive tier (and maybe other server state) still changes it, and that `--adapt-swaps 0` removes that part. We can
run more tests here if you tell us what to try.

issues.title: serve: let the image encoder run on its own GPU (vision.cuda_device)
issues.author: Efs-O
issues.body:
**Request:** let the image encoder run on its own GPU, chosen in the config, separate from the cards the engine uses.

**Why:** I have three cards: two RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB that hold the IQ3_S layer split (`"gpu": [0, 1]`) and a spare RTX 3060 12 GB. With `--vision gpu`, `strata-vision` starts with the engine's environment (`child_env(cfg)`, so `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`) and lands on card 0. It takes room the expert cache could use (the "few % slower" in the docs) while the 3060 sits idle. I couldn't find a setting for this; the env is shared at `server.py` where `Vision(cfg["vision"], ..., env=env)` is built.

**What I run locally (0.1.30):** an optional `"cuda_device"` in the config's `vision` section. When it is set, the encoder gets a copy of the env with `CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<n>` (numbered like nvidia-smi, as in #51). When it is absent, nothing changes.

```json
"vision": { "exe": "...\strata-vision.exe", "mmproj": "...", "model": "...",
            "gpu": true, "max_tokens": 1024, "cuda_device": 2 }
```

```diff
diff --git a/serve/server.py b/serve/server.py
index e03379e..e008b16 100644
--- a/serve/server.py
+++ b/serve/server.py
@@ -565,6 +565,19 @@ def child_env(cfg: dict) -> dict:
     return env
 
 
+def vision_env(cfg: dict, env: dict) -> dict:
+    """The image encoder's environment: the engine's, unless the config's vision section names its own
+    "cuda_device" (numbered like nvidia-smi) - then the encoder runs on that card alone, so a spare GPU can hold it
+    while the engine keeps every byte of its own cards."""
+    dev = (cfg.get("vision") or {}).get("cuda_device")
+    if dev is None:
+        return env
+    env = dict(env)
+    env["CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER"] = "PCI_BUS_ID"
+    env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = str(dev)
+    return env
+
+
 class ByteTokenizer:
     """Tiny stand-in tokenizer for tests without the pack: one id per UTF-8 byte, specials as ids >= 256."""
     SPECIALS = ["<|im_start|>", "<|im_end|>", "<|endoftext|>", "<|vision_start|>", "<|image_pad|>", "<|vision_end|>"]
@@ -1917,7 +1930,7 @@ def main() -> int:
         if cfg.get("vision"):
             print("loading the vision encoder ...", flush=True)
             vision = Vision(cfg["vision"], log=open(cfg["log"], "a", encoding="utf-8") if cfg.get("log") else None,
-                            env=env)
+                            env=vision_env(cfg, env))
         print("loading the model (the first start takes a minute or two) ...", flush=True)
         if len(gpu_list(cfg)) > 1:
             print(f"[strata] layer split across GPUs {gpu_list(cfg)} ({cfg.get('layer_split') or 'auto'})", flush=True)
```

Plus a unit test next to `GpuChoice.test_env`: the encoder env gets `"2"`, the engine env stays `"0,1"`, and without `cuda_device` the engine's env is returned unchanged.

**Measured (Windows 10, driver CUDA 13.0, engine 0.1.30, prebuilt `strata-vision.exe` with sm_86):**
- `nvidia-smi` shows `strata-vision.exe` on the 3060 only. The 3060 went from about 0.9 to 2.3 GB, and the two 5060 Tis stayed at about 14.9 / 15.0 GB.
- `/v1/status` reports `"vision": {"enabled": true, "available": true}`.
- A 1328×1328 PNG through `/v1/chat/completions` (`image_url` data URL) was described correctly, with 1,073 prompt tokens and 11.5 s for the full request including 151 output tokens.

**Open points for you:**
- setup.py could offer this when it finds a card outside the engine's set. I only edited the config by hand. I appended `--vision` to `args` but left out `--vram-reserve-mib`, since 700 is already the engine default.
- The encoder's card has to be in `vision_archs` (86/89/120 in the prebuilt). This patch does not check that.

Happy to open a PR if this shape works for you.
